english_verification.review_scope: Representative names, opening identity, source prose and actual fixed-revision Wiki passages, plus native national-idea text compared by localisation key. Large mission/idea ranges are locator envelopes, not exhaustive checks of every intervening line or runtime reachability.
unresolved: Mission reachability and every effect were not exhaustively audited.
No formal validator, test, build, website generation, map generation, Chinese-source, scoring, commit, or push was performed.
Current English names G60_ideas as Eltibhar Ideas, with a comment that these names are temporary pending releasable-country ideas. The Chinese source and geographic/scoring data are unchanged.

rationale.campaign_length: 44 direct G60 missions; hits in related files are not proof of additional available missions.
rationale.colonization: There are expeditions towards Amadia, but they are not the opening's main focus.
rationale.complexity: Warfare, subjects, magical investment and the event-driven endgame interlock.
rationale.dark_story: Conquest and cultural integration contain coercion, but current missions also describe coexistence policies.
rationale.difficulty: Opening battles and cross-regional prerequisites are demanding; no playtest was conducted.
rationale.diplomacy: Subject integration and the dual-empire option require managing subordinate states.
rationale.early_pressure: The Kheionai alliance creates a narrow window for the first war.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The mage estate, special alloys and army mages become central in the middle and later campaign.
rationale.narrative_density: The unifier, city conquests and Taychendi dual empire create a wide-ranging narrative.
rationale.tall_play: City rebuilding and magical workshops introduce construction prerequisites.
rationale.trade_economy: Bronze and urban production gradually enter the kingdom's supply system.
rationale.warfare: Wars against the Kheionai city-states and in Taychend form the main loop.

identity.appearance: An Eltibhar tribal kingdom in 1444, ruled by the unifier Aosiki, with its capital in province 2785.
identity.formation_scope: One endgame option changes a specified subject to J84 as a dual-empire dependency; another has G60 inherit that subject. G60 itself need not change Tag.
successors: J84 (a specified subject changes Tag in one endgame option, not a mandatory Tag change for G60)

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; racial, government and optional idea-group bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are listed separately, not stacked; accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: The western side of the island known to outsiders as Alecand is not an easy place to live. While the mountains shield us from most of the worst of the death winds, meaning we do not have to suffer the way those in the east do, our soil is still barren and rocky. However, this has taught us one thing: only the strongest and most resourceful survive, so in our raids against the easterners and each other, we will make sure we exploit the land to the fullest.

name.text: A Hardy Land, A Hardy People
name.text_en: A Hardy Land, A Hardy People

description.text: Our forts are not constructed in the style typical to elsewhere; since we do not have easy means to shear rock or make mortar ourselves, we have learned to solve the puzzle of the boulders directly. In other words, our walls are made from boulders carefully stacked together to pack tightly even without extra reinforcement. This makes our architecture not only imposing, but surprisingly sturdy.

description.text: On our island, the only sources of iron are within the territories of the easterners' cities. This has meant we lack a proper ironworking tradition. What we do have, however, is copper, and lots of it. From this we can forge bronze, and thanks to our long tradition of working with it as well as having to make sure it can compete with eastern metallurgic developments, means our bronze is stronger than any one might find elsewhere.

description.text: Since time immemorial our people have gotten together to compete against each other in brotherhood. When we weren't raiding each other before unification, we would come together in great festivals to show off our martial prowess to each other. It has been suggested that we formalize these festivals, known as the Ghílti Kanvrenu in our language, and hold one every year so that our greatest warriors and strategists can be shown off for all to see.

description.text: It was a solemn affair. The greatest generals and nobles of our nation were lined up in the best finery. Our priests practiced their holiest rites. And at the center of it all, our chieftain. But as the crown fell on their head, they were no longer just a mere chieftain: they were now the first king, Riei, of all the Eltikani people.

description.text: Rigòti, the greatest peak on our island. Our holy protector from the winds of death. So ubiquitous and quintessential to everyone's way of life, the easterners simply call it Meteí, ‘The Mountain', for it needs no other name. For eons our people have climbed this mountain to seek holy wisdom and enlightenment from its embrace. At the urging of our priests, we will establish waystations along the disparate paths up its cliffs and valleys to ensure all of our people who wish to may glimpse even a fragment of the divine.

description.text: As we have begun to engage in contact with the outside world, we have started to realize something: nobody else speaks quite like we do. Even those from the eastern shores have extreme difficulty understanding our sentences. While this does mean many foreign diplomats dread being assigned to our court and having to master our way of speaking, the same also applies to their spies, making it easier for us to make sure that things we want to be secret, stay secret.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you dislike a demanding first war or sustained later expansion and magical-industrial prerequisites.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Break through the Kheionai alliance, integrate cities through subjects and land rights, then build a mage army and decide Taychend's political future.
player_overview.overview: In 1444 Eltikan has united western Alecand's tribes and commands land and cavalry, but faces a Kheionai city-state alliance. Use pilgrimage and military opportunities to win the first war, or integrate cities gradually through subjects. Then grant the conquered land rights, build magical workshops and push into Taychend. The ending can make a specified subject the Taychendi Empire or let you inherit it: it does not inevitably change the player to J84. A forceful opening and cross-regional governance define the campaign.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy aggressive cavalry warfare, subject integration, urban governance and cross-regional epic campaigns.
signature_features: Boar cavalry and bronze equipment give the tribal kingdom a high-pressure opening.
Several missions establish subjects before inheritance, combining war with political integration.
The Taychendi ending can create a J84 dual-empire subject or have G60 inherit it directly.
player_overview.tagline: Break through with western Alecand's unifier and boar cavalry, then command the fate of cities, magical forges and Taychend.

reasons: A distinctive opening of boar cavalry and tribal unification.
City integration through subject formation followed by inheritance.
Magical forges and the dual-empire endgame mark major transitions.
warnings: High pressure in the first war and pilgrimage window.
In one ending J84 is the subject's new Tag, not an automatic G60 succession.

phase_scores.phase: Proof through warfare and tribal conquest
Integration through land rights and shared festivals

positive_indicators: Land rights granted to Kheionai urban nobles
The Taychendi endgame advocates shared prosperity and fellowship across peoples
values.rationale: Land rights for city residents, shared festivals, rebuilding and cross-cultural representation provide substantive positive evidence. Coercive subject relations, destructive rhetoric against political rivals and military victory as proof of legitimacy limit restraint. The representative missions do not establish systematic extermination.
red_flags: Rule established through war and pressure on subjects
